learn.title: 17 · Reference solution

designClaim: a semaphore of 2 for hydrogen, 1 for oxygen and a barrier of 3; each thread takes its slot, waits at the barrier, prints, and only then gives the slot back
solutionMd:
## The idea

Two rules. **At most 2 hydrogens and 1 oxygen** may be in the molecule being formed — two semaphores. And the three must **wait for each other** — a barrier for 3. The subtle part: give your semaphore slot back only **after** you have been released, so the next molecule cannot finish in the middle of this one.

## Step by step

1. Hydrogen: wait on the H semaphore (2 slots).
2. Wait at the barrier until 3 threads (2 H + 1 O) have arrived.
3. Call releaseHydrogen().
4. Release the H slot.
5. Oxygen: the same with the O semaphore (1 slot).

## Worked example

**Input:** arrivals O, H, H, H, O, H

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| O, H, H | take slots, meet at the barrier → print O, H, H in some order |
| next H | waits for an H slot until this molecule's H has printed |
| H, O, H | second molecule forms and prints |

**Result:** output like "OHH HOH" — every group of three is two H and one O

## Cost

Each molecule costs one barrier phase; no busy-waiting.

## The code (C#, compiled and tested against every part of the question)

```csharp
// LeetCode 1117 — threads arrive as hydrogen or oxygen; let them through in groups of exactly 2 H + 1 O.
public sealed class H2O {
    private readonly SemaphoreSlim _hydrogen = new SemaphoreSlim(2, 2);   // at most 2 H in the current molecule
    private readonly SemaphoreSlim _oxygen = new SemaphoreSlim(1, 1);     // at most 1 O
    private readonly Barrier _barrier = new Barrier(3);                   // wait until all three are present

    public void Hydrogen(Action releaseHydrogen) {
        _hydrogen.Wait();
        _barrier.SignalAndWait();     // the molecule is complete
        releaseHydrogen();
        _hydrogen.Release();          // release the slot only AFTER printing, so the next molecule
    }                                 // cannot finish before this one has printed

    public void Oxygen(Action releaseOxygen) {
        _oxygen.Wait();
        _barrier.SignalAndWait();
        releaseOxygen();
        _oxygen.Release();
    }
}
```

## Likely follow-up questions

**Q: Why release after printing?**

Otherwise a new H can take the freed slot, complete the next barrier and print before this molecule's last thread prints.

**Q: Cost?**

Each molecule costs one barrier phase — fine. Throughput is bounded by the barrier, not the semaphores.

**Q: Without a Barrier class?**

A lock with counters of waiting H and O and Monitor.PulseAll when a molecule can form — more code, more ways to miss a wake-up.

**Q: Groups of different shapes (e.g. CO₂).**

Generalise: one semaphore per kind sized to its count, a barrier sized to the molecule.

**Q: How do you test concurrency code?**

Many random arrival orders, a timeout to catch deadlocks, and checking the invariant on the output — as these tests do.
